newsitem.title: UK: BOC SEEN REPORTING FLAT TO LOWER Q3.
newsitem.headline: BOC SEEN REPORTING FLAT TO LOWER Q3.

text.p: British specialist gases company BOC Group Plc is expected to announce flat to slightly lower nine-month profit figures on August 12 as the impact of the stronger pound masks modest underlying progress, analysts said on Friday.
The company is expected to report profits little changed from the 327.3 million stg announced a year earlier.
David Ingles, analyst at HSBC James Capel, who is expecting profit of around 328 million stg, said the main impact on BOC would be the translation of overseas profits back into sterling.
Ingles said the company had been affected by the weakness of the South African rand, with sterling's rise against the U.S. and Australian dollars and Japanese yen also important factors.

Kleinwort Benson's Michael Eastwood, who is expecting pre-tax profit for the nine months of 322.4 million stg, said the pound's strength is likely to have wiped up to 14 million pounds off profits in the third-quarter.
Analysts said the core industrial gases business is expected to have continued to see steady growth.

Recovery at the vacuum operation, which provides super clean environments for specialist sectors such as semiconductor makers, is likely to be most vulnerable to the rise of the pound as an exporter from the UK.
Healthcare division Ohmeda will be a major focus of interest after the company announced on July 23 that the underperforming medical gases and critical monitoring business was up for sale.
"The attention is really on this earnings enhancing disposal," said Nikko Europe analyst Philip Morrish.

Morrish said he would be interested to see how much detail the company gave on Ohmeda, which is expected to fetch between 500 million stg and 1 billion stg. A prospectus is currently being prepared for potential buyers.
Britain's Zeneca Group Plc indicated on Thursday that it might be interested in all or part of Ohmeda, which is geared up to make a generic competitor to Zeneca's Diprivan anaesthetic from 1999.
